questions.question: Which metal ion released from tannery industry causes acute water pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cr.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chromium**:-

 
 
• **The metal ion released from tannery industry that causes acute water pollution is chromium (Cr).**
 
• Chromium is a heavy metal and a toxic pollutant that can cause severe health problems such as cancer, liver and kidney damage, and respiratory issues.
 
• **Tannery industry uses chromium in the form of chromium salts as a tanning agent to process animal hides and skins into leather.**
 
• The wastewater generated from tannery industry contains high levels of chromium, which is discharged into water bodies without proper treatment, leading to acute water pollution. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnesium (Mg):-**

 
 
• ​__It is an essential mineral that is commonly found in water and soil. It is not considered a toxic pollutant and does not cause acute water pollution.
 
 
 
• **Arsenic**:-
 
 
• As is a toxic metalloid that can cause serious health problems such as skin lesions, cancer, and cardiovascular disease. It is commonly found in groundwater in some regions, but it is not directly related to tannery industry pollution.
 
 
 
• **Zinc:-**
 
 
• Zn is a trace element that is essential for human health and is commonly found in water and soil. It is not considered a toxic pollutant and does not cause acute water pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations launched the 'United for Biodiversity' coalition made up of zoos, aquariums, botanical gardens, national parks, natural history, and science museums from around the world, on World Wildlife Day 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__European Commission.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **European Commission** has launched the** 'United for Biodiversity'** coalition made up of zoos, aquariums, botanical gardens, national parks, natural history and science museums from around the world, on** World Wildlife Day 2020.**
 
• The European Commission has put forward plans for the world's first** "carbon border tax"** on imports of carbon-intensive goods, including steel, cement, fertilizers, and aluminium, as part of a program to meet its new climate target.
 
• The border levy should be phased in from** 2026.**
 
• The measure is designed to protect European industries from competitors abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Health Organization:**

 
 
• World Health Organization (WHO) is a** specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) established in 1948 **to further international cooperation for improved public health conditions.
 
• Although it inherited specific tasks relating to epidemic control, quarantine measures, and drug standardization from the** Health Organization of the League of Nations (set up in 1923) and the International Office of Public Health at Paris (established in 1907),** WHO was given a broad mandate under its constitution to promote the attainment of "the highest possible level of health" by all peoples.
 
• WHO defines health positively as **"a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity."**
 
• Each year WHO celebrates its date of establishment,** April 7, 1948, as World Health Day.**
 
• With administrative headquarters in **Geneva, governance of WHO operates through the World Health Assembly**, which meets annually as the general policy-making body, and through an Executive Board of health specialists elected for three-year terms by the assembly.
 
• **The WHO Secretariat,** which carries out routine operations and helps implement strategies, consists of experts, staff, and field workers who have appointments at the central headquarters or at one of the six regional WHO offices or other offices located in countries around the world.

questions.question: In which year was the National Biodiversity Authority, a statutory autonomous body, established under the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Biodiversity Authority**

 
 
• After signing the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in 1992**, India formed the **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), a statutory autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Environment, Forests, and Climate Change, in 2003**.
 
• It was **made to carry out the requirements of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002**.
 
• It serves as **facilitation, regulation, and advisory body to the Indian government "on issues of conservation, sustainable use of biological resources**, and fair and equitable distribution of benefits emerging from the use of biological resources."
 
• Its main office is in **Chennai, India**.
 
• Additionally, it provides **guidance to State Governments in designating biodiversity hotspots **as heritage monuments.
 
• **NBA** held the **first-ever National Biodiversity Congress (NBC) in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, in 2012**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Since its founding, NBA has supported the development of **State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) in 29 States **and aided the construction of approximately **1,39,831 Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)**.
 
• The **National Biodiversity Authority** is charged with controlling access to biological resources and/or related knowledge for research, bio-survey, and commercial use, as well as obtaining intellectual property rights, transferring research findings, and transferring accessed biological resources.
 
• On the **website of the National Biodiversity Authority** there are the details of the **application forms for Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS)** of particular activities.
 
• The current **chairperson** of **NBA** is **Dr. V. B. Mathur**.

questions.question: What is the importance of the ozone layer for life on Earth?

options.text: It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.
It protects us from acidic rainfall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ozone layer is one of the layers in the earth's atmosphere inside the stratosphere layer. It absorbs ultraviolet radiation and protects people, animals, plants, and marine life from the sun's harmful rays.
 
• It was discovered by** Charles Fabry and Henri Buisson in 1913.**
 
• It can** absorb 98% of the sun's ultraviolet rays and almost 90% of ozone is located in the stratosphere layer at a distance of 15 to 30 km from the surface of Earth.**
 
• **In 1989, the Montreal protocol **came to protect the ozone layer by cutting the substances that deplete the ozone layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone:**

 
 
• It is important to mankind because it creates a protective coverage against ultraviolet rays.
 
• **Formula Ozone is O₃.**
 
• The ozone layer is found in the stratosphere. The stratosphere is the mass of protective gases clinging to our planet. The ozone layer acts as a shield for life on Earth.
 
• The ozone layer only makes **up 0.00006 per cent **of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• The ozone layer is getting thinner because of chemicals called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). Due to this reason nowadays hydrochlorofluorocarbons **(HCFCs) are used in place of CFCs.**
 
• **CFCs are non-toxic, nonflammable chemicals containing atoms of carbon, chlorine, and fluorine.**
 
• **"Ozone holes”** are popular names for areas of damage to the ozone layer.
 
• **The ozone layer is thinnest near the poles due to very low temperatures.**

questions.question: A pyramid of biomass is a diagram that shows the population at each level of the food chain. Accordingly, ________ occupy the base with the highest biomass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **pyramid** of biomass is a graphical representation that shows the population at each level of the food chain. 
 
• **Producers** occupy the base with the highest biomass.
 
• The relationship between numbers, biomass, energy, or bio productivity of an ecosystem can be represented by a pyramid known as the **ecological pyramid.**
 
• **The trophic level **is the place that a living organism occupies in a food chain.
 
• In a biomass pyramid, **producers** are at the base, followed by **herbivores** and then **carnivores** at the top.
 
• The **pyramid** of biomass shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
 
• **10 percent** of the energy gets transferred to the next trophic level and the rest is either utilized for metabolic processes or excreted out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carnivores that eat herbivores are called** secondary consumers**.
 
• A separate trophic level, the **decomposers** or transformers, consists of organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead organisms and waste materials into nutrients usable by the producers.
 
• **Primary consumers** make up the second trophic level. They are also called herbivores.

questions.question: Which ecologist’s research provided revolutionary new insights into how energy and nutrients move through the ecosystems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raymond L Lindeman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raymond Laurel Lindeman **(**1915 – June 29, 1942**) was an **ecologist **whose **graduate research **is **credited with being a seminal study in **the **field of ecosystem ecology**, **specifically **on the **topic of trophic dynamics**.
 
• **Lindeman completed **his **Ph.D**. at the **University of Minnesota **with his **thesis work **being concerned with the history and ecological dynamics of Cedar Bog Lake.
 
• **Some insights **of his research:
 
 
• **Energy is passed from one trophic level **to the **next trophic level**.
 
• Hence, **energy flows **in one **direction **through **successive trophic levels **in **a food chain**.
 
• **Nutrients **are **produced from the matter**. The **matter **may be **organic **or **inorganic**.
 
• The **organic **and **inorganic matter **is produced, exchanged, and moved within the **ecosystem **and this is **called cycling**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Arthur George Tansley **FLS, FRS (**15 August 1871 – 25 November 1955**) was an **English botanist **and a **pioneer **in the science of ecology.
 
• **Ernst Heinrich Philipp August Haeckel **was a **German zoologist**, **naturalist**, **eugenicist**, **philosopher**, **physician**, **professor**, **marine biologist, and artist**.
 
• **Charles Sutherland **Elton FRS (**29 March 1900 – 1 May 1991**) was an **English zoologist **and **animal ecologist**.

__
 
• **The Indian Ocean tsunami is **also known as the** Christmas or Boxing Day tsunami.**
 
• It took place in** 2004**.
 
• **The Sumatra-Andaman earthquake** is estimated to have** released energy equivalent to 23,000 Hiroshima-type atomic bombs.**
 
• The Sumatra-Andaman earthquake struck** 241.40 km** (**150 miles)** from the coast of **Sumatra island**, in the northwest of the** Indonesian island group, and 49.88 km (31 miles) below the ocean floor.**
 
• The magnitude 9.1 quake** ruptured a ****1500 km **( **900-mile) stretch of fault line** where the** Indian and Australian tectonic plates meet.**
 
• It was a powerful megathrust quake, occurring where a** heavy ocean plate slips under a lighter continental plate**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is mainly responsible for the increase in the greenhouse effect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increasing CO2 concentration**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Increasing CO2 concentration** is the primary factor contributing to the enhancement of the greenhouse effect.
 
• The greenhouse effect is a natural phenomenon where certain gases in the Earth's atmosphere trap heat, preventing it from escaping into space and thereby warming the planet.
 
• Human activities, particularly the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas, have significantly increased the concentration of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the atmosphere.
 
• This rise in CO2 levels enhances the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change.
 
• Other greenhouse gases include methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and fluorinated gases, but CO2 is the most abundant and has the most significant impact.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SO2 levels** (Sulfur dioxide) primarily contribute to acid rain rather than the greenhouse effect.
 
• **Ozone layer hole** refers to the depletion of the ozone layer, which protects the Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation, but it is not a primary factor in the greenhouse effect.
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** are potent greenhouse gases and also contribute to ozone layer depletion, but their concentration is much lower compared to CO2.
 
• Efforts to mitigate climate change focus on reducing CO2 emissions through renewable energy sources, energy efficiency, reforestation, and other measures.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• DDT is **very insoluble in water and very persistent in the environment, making it a highly polluting hazard**.
 
• Its half-life has been reported to be between **2 and 15 years.**
 
• DDT (dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane) was developed as the first of the **modern synthetic insecticides** in the 1940s.
 
• It was initially used with great effect to **combat malaria, typhus, and other insect-borne human diseases among both military and civilian populations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Insecticides are **chemicals used to control insects by killing them or preventing them from engaging in undesirable or destructive behaviours**.
 
• Organic pesticides are usually considered as those **pesticides that come from natural sources**. 
 
• Synthetic** contact insecticides** are now the **primary agents of insect control**.​ 
 
• Inorganic insecticides are **of mineral origin, mainly compounds of antimony, arsenic, barium, boron, copper, fluorine, mercury, selenium, sulfur, thallium, and zinc, and elemental phosphorus and sulfur**.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following statements about eutrophication is correct?

options.text: It happens when too less nitrogen is present in the water, causing reduced growth of plants and algae.
It is a beneficial process for environment restoration.
It happens when too much nitrogen enriches the water, causing excessive growth of plants and algae.
It happens when too much carbon enriches the water, causing excessive growth of bacteria and reduced growth of plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It happens when too much nitrogen enriches the water, causing excessive growth of plants and algae.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is a process where water bodies become enriched with nutrients, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus.
 
• This nutrient enrichment leads to **excessive growth of algae and aquatic plants**, which can result in harmful algal blooms.
 
• These algal blooms can deplete oxygen levels in the water, causing **dead zones** where aquatic life cannot survive.
 
• The primary sources of nutrients causing eutrophication include agricultural runoff, wastewater discharge, and industrial effluents.
 
• Eutrophication can lead to a loss of biodiversity, changes in species composition and dominance, and overall deterioration of water quality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preventive measures** include reducing nutrient runoff through better agricultural practices, improving sewage treatment facilities, and implementing policies to control industrial discharges.
 
• Restoration efforts for eutrophic water bodies may involve **mechanical, chemical, or biological methods** to remove excess nutrients and restore ecological balance.
 
• Public awareness and education about the sources and impacts of eutrophication are crucial for long-term water quality management.
 
• International cooperation and regulations, such as the European Union's Water Framework Directive, play a vital role in addressing transboundary water pollution issues.

questions.question: What was the name of the oldest female black rhino which died in 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Fausta__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fausta, a female black rhino, who was believed to be the world’s oldest rhino has died at the age of 57 in a Tanzanian conservation area**__.

 __
 
• Fausta died of** natural causes in captivity in Ngorongoro Crater, **which lies in the Ngorongoro Conservation Area of **Tanzania**.
 
• **Fausta was first located in 1965 at the age of between 3 and 4 years old by a scientist.**
 
 
• However, Fausta survived 57 years without bearing calves.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Black rhinoceros**

 
 
• **They are also called ‘hook-lipped rhinoceros’. **

 
 
• This species of rhinoceros although is referred to as ‘black’, but its colours vary from brown to grey.
 
 
 
• **They are smaller of two African species (the other being the white rhinoceros’ species) and are found around south and east Africa, including Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe.**
 
 
 
• **IUCN Status: **
 
 
• **Critically endangered; (although South-western black rhinoceros is classified as vulnerable).**
 
 
 
• According to charity ‘Save The Rhino’, Black rhinos who are now decimated by poaching, now numbers only around 5,500.

questions.question: Which of the following watershed development projects is sponsored by the Central Government aims at enabling the rural population to conserve water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Haryali.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hariyali is a watershed development and management program implemented by the central and state governments**.
 
• The project is being implemented at the** Grama Panchayat level** with people's participation.
 
• The main **objectives** of the Hariyali program are:
 
 
• Harvesting every drop of rainwater for purposes of irrigation, plantations to create sustainable sources of income for the village community as well as for drinking water supplies.
 
• Overall development of rural areas by creating regular sources of income for the Panchayat from rainwater harvesting and management.
 
• Employment generation and poverty alleviation in rural areas.
 
• All the district level, ZP/DRDA shall be the nodal authority for the implementation of all the area development programs under the supervision and guidance of the State Government and the Government of India.
 
• A meeting of the Gram Sabha/ Ward Sabha shall be convened for the preparation of the Action Plan/Watershed Treatment Plan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gram Panchayat shall maintain a separate account for the watershed project and all receipts from ZP/DRDA will be credited to this account.
 
• The Gram Panchayat shall constitute Self Help Groups (SHGs) in the watershed area.
 
• **Neeru-Meeru** is a programme in Andhra Pradesh was taken up constructions of various water harvesting structures dug out ponds, check dams through people participation.
 
• **Arvary Pani Sansad programme **is associated with Rajasthan.

questions.question: Which of the following environmental movements/conflicts of India was directly related to the prevention of felling of trees?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Chipko Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chipko movement was the uprising against the felling of trees and sustaining the ecological balance started in Uttar Pradesh’s Chamoli district (now Uttarakhand) in 1973.**
 
• The name of the movement ‘chipko’ comes from the word ’embrace’. Hugged the trees and encircled them to prevent being hacked.
 
• Sundarlal Bahuguna, a famous Gandhian, is said to have started this movement to guard the trees on the Himalayan slopes. Bahuguna is also known for coining the Chipko slogan **‘ecology is the permanent economy’.**
 
• The movement’s biggest victory was making people aware of their rights to forests, and how grassroots activism can influence policy-making regarding ecology and shared natural resources.
 
• It was a silent, non-violent protest condemning ecological destruction.

questions.question: Select the natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir forest**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gir forest** is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica).
 
• Located in the state of **Gujarat, India**, the Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is the last refuge of the Asiatic Lion.
 
• The park was established in **1965** and covers a total area of **1,412 square kilometers**.
 
• Conservation efforts in Gir have been successful in increasing the population of Asiatic Lions from a mere **20 in the early 20th century** to over **500 today**.
 
• The ecosystem of Gir forest is unique, supporting a rich biodiversity that includes leopards, deer, antelopes, and numerous bird species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Asiatic Lion** once roamed across the Middle East and India but is now restricted to the Gir forest.
 
• The Government of India and the Gujarat state government have implemented several **conservation programs** to protect the Asiatic Lion.
 
• In addition to Gir, there are efforts to identify and establish **alternative habitats** to ensure a healthy and genetically diverse population.
 
• The Gir forest is also a significant cultural and historical site, attracting numerous **tourists** and wildlife enthusiasts from around the world.
